sources.note: Nothing; it is a bibliography. It lists for Vivti exactly the three wordlist resources already in our bibliography (Shimelman 2015 ABVD id 1253; Vanuatu Voices Fifti: Khatbol and Fifti: Malmbor) and no grammar, sketch, phonology, text or thesis; Nitita likewise has only ABVD + Vanuatu Voices wordlists. Independent confirmation that our Vivti list is complete on the descriptive side and that Crowley's 2004 wordlist and Keating 2007 are the only further leads.

sources.citation: Crowley, Terry. 2006. The Avava language of central Malakula (Vanuatu). Ed. John Lynch. Pacific Linguistics 574. Canberra: ANU. Introduction pp. 6-7, 12-13; Phonology sec. 2.3 pp. 36-37.
sources.note: Glottolog's only descriptive reference for Vivti. Names the language, locates it (Vanakh, SE/E slopes of Levarmas peak), counts <20 speakers in Khatbol in 2004, gives 11 comparative lexical items and states it is 'completely unrepresented in published sources, though in 2004 I was able to record approximately 500 words'. No Vivti phonology; nothing about Vivti stress. Sec. 2.3 p.36 describes AVAVA stress (penultimate; final closed syllable with diphthong/long vowel stressed) and says only that Avava 'appears to follow the pattern that is encountered in most of the neighbouring languages'.
